newsitem.title: USA: Widening arb seen fueling Brent trade into US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Widening arb seen fueling Brent trade into US Gulf.

text.p: The trans-Atlantic arbitrage moved out on Wednesday, raising expectations that more North Sea Brent crude would head toward the U.S. Gulf Coast in August, traders said.
The August spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent was around $1.35-40 a barrel on Wednesday afternoon, up from $1.25-30 a barrel on Tuesday.
"August WTI/Brent widened by about 10 cents, so that means you'll see more crude coming over," said one Gulf Coast buyer.
On Tuesday, a Norwegian company sold the last of four Brent cargoes to a Gulf Coast refiner at August WTI minus 30-35 cents a barrel for August 10-15 delivery.
West African offerings were plentiful, traders said.
A U.S. refiner picked up an Odudu cargo arriving in mid-August for around 50 cents off WTI, traders said.
Qua Iboe for first-half August delivery was on offer at around $1.85-95 a barrel over Dated Brent, while Forcados was looking for a home at a premium of around $1.75 a barrel, traders said.
A European company was showing Palanca, loading in July, at an fob price of Dated Brent plus 20 cents a barrel.
The same firm was also showing Rabi Light and N'Kossa loading in mid-August, traders said.
From Latin America, Colombian Cusiana was on offer around 80-90 cents under WTI for early August loading.
Among other Colombian grades, a European company was showing Cano Limon loading August 17-23, asking $2.30 a barrel under WTI.
The same firm was offering Vasconia loading August 6-10, asking a discount of $3.06 a barrel.
A trading house had another Vasconia cargo loading August 14-19, traders said.
Elsewhere in the region, traders were awaiting the results of a Chilean tender to purchase 960,000 barrel of crude for August 14-18 delivery. Bids were due today.
